def: Able to develop into several related cell types but not all of them. Hematopoietic stem cells are multipotent, giving rise to all blood cell lines.

Disordered, ineffective blood cell production in the bone marrow, leading to low blood counts and risk of leukemia (myelodysplastic syndromes). On some cards it also refers to malformed spinal cord, as in spina bifida.
An imaging test in which contrast dye is injected into the spinal canal, then imaged by X-ray or CT, to show compression of the spinal cord or nerve roots.
A severe neural tube defect in which an exposed, flat plate of spinal cord tissue lies open on the back without a covering sac. It is a form of spina bifida.
Suppressing bone marrow activity, lowering blood cell counts. Chemotherapy, azathioprine and chloramphenicol are myelosuppressive and cause anemia, infection risk and bleeding.
A brief ridge of muscle that rises when the muscle is tapped, because of delayed relaxation. It is classically seen in severe hypothyroidism.
Inflammation of the heart muscle and surrounding pericardium together, usually viral. It causes chest pain, ST elevation and raised troponin.
A small surgical incision in the eardrum to drain fluid or pus from the middle ear, often with a tympanostomy tube placed for recurrent otitis media.
A topical allylamine antifungal that inhibits squalene epoxidase, blocking ergosterol synthesis. It treats tinea infections such as athlete's foot.
Relating to the nasociliary nerve, a branch of the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve (V1). It carries sensation from the nose and cornea and is the afferent limb of the corneal reflex.
A new bladder surgically built from a segment of intestine after bladder removal (cystectomy), usually for bladder cancer.
Brand of over-the-counter antibiotic ointment containing neomycin, bacitracin and polymyxin B, used on minor skin wounds. It can cause contact dermatitis, especially from neomycin.
Capable of causing glomerulonephritis. Nephritogenic strains of group A streptococcus cause poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.
Formation of the kidney during development, ending around 36 weeks of gestation. Premature birth interrupts it and can leave fewer nephrons.
Relating to the central neuraxis, the brain and spinal cord. Neuraxial anesthesia (spinal or epidural) puts anesthetic around the spinal cord.
Progressive joint destruction caused by loss of pain and position sense in a neuropathic joint (Charcot joint). Diabetes mellitus is the most common cause; syphilis and syringomyelia are others.
Caused by too little glucose reaching the brain. Neuroglycopenic symptoms of hypoglycemia include confusion, weakness, seizures and loss of consciousness.
Able to invade the nervous system. West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease causes meningitis, encephalitis or acute flaccid paralysis.
Dark pigment in catecholamine neurons, notably the substantia nigra and locus ceruleus. Loss of pigmented nigral neurons marks Parkinson disease.
One of two temporary openings at the ends of the neural tube in the embryo. Failure of the anterior neuropore to close causes anencephaly; the posterior causes spina bifida.
The two openings at the ends of the embryonic neural tube. Failure of the anterior neuropore to close causes anencephaly; failure of the posterior causes spina bifida.
Involvement of the nervous system by sarcoidosis, with granulomas causing cranial neuropathies (especially facial nerve palsy), meningitis or hypothalamic disease.
A tyrosine kinase inhibitor (blocking VEGF, FGF and PDGF receptors) used to slow lung function decline in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
Describes severe acne with deep inflamed nodules and cysts that can scar. It is treated with isotretinoin.
Peptides made of nine amino acids. Oxytocin and antidiuretic hormone (vasopressin) are both nonapeptides made in the hypothalamus.
Not turning pale when pressed. Nonblanching skin lesions such as petechiae and purpura mean blood has leaked from vessels, as in meningococcemia or thrombocytopenia.
An oxygen mask with a reservoir bag and one-way valves that prevent exhaled air from being rebreathed. It delivers high-concentration oxygen, up to about 90 percent.
Describes germ cell tumors other than pure seminoma, such as embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma and teratoma. They often raise alpha-fetoprotein or beta-hCG.
Coin-shaped. Nummular eczema forms round, scaly, itchy patches on the skin.
A reduced level of alertness, with drowsiness and slowed response to stimulation, but not full unconsciousness. It lies between lethargy and stupor.
Having reduced alertness and slowed responses, between lethargic and stuporous, though not completely unconscious.
A fetal position in which the back of the baby's head (occiput) faces the mother's spine, so the baby is born face up. It can prolong labor and cause back pain.
Involving the eye and nearby lymph glands. Parinaud oculoglandular syndrome is conjunctivitis with swollen preauricular nodes, classically from cat-scratch disease (Bartonella).
Arthritis affecting four or fewer joints. It is seen in juvenile idiopathic arthritis and reactive arthritis.
Infrequent ovulation, leading to irregular or sparse menstrual periods. It is a feature of polycystic ovary syndrome.
A short carbohydrate chain of a few sugar units. Oligosaccharides are attached to proteins in glycosylation, and some are not digested until bacteria ferment them in the colon.
A long-acting inhaled beta-2 agonist that relaxes airway smooth muscle, used as maintenance treatment of COPD.
The larval stage of tapeworms, a six-hooked embryo inside the egg. Swallowed eggs release oncospheres that penetrate the gut, as in cysticercosis from Taenia solium.
A lid or covering flap. In the brain it is cortex covering the insula; in the cervix, the mucus plug; in dentistry, gum over an erupting tooth.
Describes severe backward arching of the head, neck and spine from muscle spasm, seen in tetanus, strychnine poisoning and some brain injuries.
A severe backward arching of the head, neck and spine from muscle spasm. It is seen in tetanus, strychnine poisoning and severe meningitis or brain injury.
A recombinant form of interleukin-11 that stimulates platelet production. It was used to prevent thrombocytopenia after chemotherapy and can cause fluid retention.
The nucleotide (orotidine monophosphate) made from orotic acid in pyrimidine synthesis. Buildup of orotic acid from enzyme deficiency causes hereditary orotic aciduria.
Braces or supports applied to the body to correct, protect or support a limb or joint, such as ankle-foot orthoses for foot drop.
The illusion that the visual world is bouncing or shaking, caused by involuntary eye movements such as nystagmus or loss of vestibular function.
A small molecule, such as sorbitol, taurine or betaine, that cells accumulate to balance osmotic pressure without disrupting proteins.
Small molecules such as sorbitol, taurine and betaine that cells accumulate to balance osmotic pressure without disrupting protein function.
Involving both bone and its overlying articular cartilage. An osteochondral defect is a damaged area of joint surface and underlying bone.
Syphilis involving the ear, causing hearing loss, tinnitus and vertigo. It can occur at any stage of syphilis.
